original.purpose: Cover run registration, bounded event collection, decode integration, and cleanup of the audit daemon PID.
original.reason: Requires a disposable audit-enabled VM with CAP_AUDIT_READ and CAP_AUDIT_WRITE, no competing audit daemon, controlled fixture-owned syscall event generation, and a snapshot/restore procedure for daemon PID and audit state. No daemon or netlink operation was invoked here.

entries.current_reason: Consuming events requires being the registered audit daemon (CAP_AUDIT_CONTROL, initial user+PID ns, no competing auditd), a controller-installed rule, fixture-triggered events and pid/enabled restore. An unprivileged fixture cannot observe the obligation: audit_netlink_ok() returns ECONNREFUSED in any non-initial user namespace (legacy bwrap, USERNS) and EPERM for uid 2000 without CAP_AUDIT_CONTROL in the plain driver; audit state is global, not namespaced.

entries.notes: KERNEL: audit_netlink_ok() (kernel/audit.c, 6.12) returns ECONNREFUSED for any caller outside the initial user namespace and EPERM for AUDIT_GET/SET/LIST_RULES/ADD_RULE/DEL_RULE outside the initial PID namespace or without CAP_AUDIT_CONTROL. original.purpose: Verify deterministic clock-domain sentinels and special timestamp boundaries using injected readings.
original.reason: Requires a disposable VM or reviewed clock_gettime mock returning distinct fixed REALTIME/MONOTONIC/BOOTTIME sentinels and boundary nanoseconds. Live domain reads execute with independent Python bounds separately; injected-sample results remain deferred.

entries.current_reason: clock_gettime is served by the vDSO in both builds, so seccomp cannot intercept it; deterministic sample injection needs a build-time test hook or ptrace/vDSO interposition. A user+time namespace (unprivileged in the VM plain driver if user namespaces are enabled) can offset CLOCK_MONOTONIC and CLOCK_BOOTTIME by chosen amounts but not CLOCK_REALTIME. Domain identity is closable unprivileged with a time namespace; boundary sentinels need a clock-injection capability.

requirements.behavior: now/mono/boot read REALTIME/MONOTONIC/BOOTTIME respectively (domain identity).

evidence.assertion: each read lies between independent Python clock_gettime_ns samples of the documented domain

requirements.gap: In a live VM the monotonic and boottime clocks differ only by suspend time (none), so brackets cannot distinguish mono from boot; distinct domain offsets are not exercised.

requirements.behavior: Output format: fixed nine fractional digits.

evidence.assertion: nine fractional digits and non-decreasing samples
fixed-width formatting of now/mono/boot

requirements.behavior: Special timestamp boundaries (zero seconds, nanosecond 0 and 999999999, negative/large epochs).
requirements.gap: Cannot be produced from live clocks; requires injected samples.

entries.notes: bashclock.c:115 clock_gettime.

original.purpose: Check clock_nanosleep EINTR handling and non-EINTR syscall error diagnostics.
original.reason: Requires a disposable VM with a deterministic signal/timer driver or reviewed clock_nanosleep mock to inject EINTR and a distinct syscall failure. The successful GNU-parity cases do not cover these error paths, and this suite does not execute or claim them passed.

entries.current_reason: EINTR is observable now, and a distinct clock_nanosleep failure is reachable with a stateless per-side seccomp RET_ERRNO filter. Neither needs a new driver.

requirements.behavior: A signal that interrupts `bashclock sleep` (EINTR) makes it return failure without a spurious diagnostic, honouring SIGINT/handlers.
requirements.gap: Not executed; reproducible unprivileged: an owned child sends USR1 (trapped) to $$ during `bashclock sleep 2`. requirements.behavior: --remount -o ro DST (and -o rw) changes an existing mount's flags; super-block versus per-mount effects are compared with util-linux `mount -o remount,ro`.

requirements.gap: No case invokes these parse paths. Usage checks need no privilege but are still unexecuted.

entries.notes: Semantic difference to check: bashmount --remount passes MS_REMOUNT|flags without MS_BIND (bashmount.c:680-686), which changes super-block flags. util-linux `mount -o remount,ro` on a bind mount uses MS_REMOUNT|MS_BIND in libmount, which changes the per-mount flag only. A remount of a bind target may therefore diverge (unexecuted prediction).

original.purpose: Exercise plain typed mounts, option flag mapping, and filesystem-specific data forwarding.
original.reason: Requires a disposable VM with a dedicated mount namespace and disposable tmpfs target, or a reviewed mount(2) mock that records source, target, type, flags, and data. The fixture must verify successful tmpfs mount effects and option combinations such as ro,nosuid,size=64k without touching host mounts.

entries.current_reason: Missing fixture. No executed case attempts a mount. In the existing drivers uid 2000 gets EPERM from mount(2), but a fresh user plus mount namespace (USERNS) gives namespace-scoped CAP_SYS_ADMIN, enough for tmpfs mounts, binds, remounts and lazy unmounts of mounts created there. Locked-flag rules apply only to mounts inherited from the parent namespace, so use fresh tmpfs mounts.

requirements.behavior: A plain typed mount of a tmpfs onto a relative directory succeeds; afterwards the target is a mountpoint of fstype tmpfs, and files written into it live on the new filesystem.
requirements.gap: No executed case calls bashmount SRC DST. The suite's queries (mountpoint_devno, nonmount-device-query) never create a mount.

requirements.behavior: Known option names map to MS_* flags: -o ro,nosuid,nodev,noexec,noatime yields the matching per-mount options in mountinfo, and rw/suid/dev/exec clear the opposite bits.
requirements.gap: No mount runs, so no mountinfo option string is produced or compared.

requirements.behavior: Unknown option tokens are forwarded as filesystem data. With -o size=64k the tmpfs super options show size=64k, combined with the ro,nosuid flag mapping in the same request.
requirements.gap: Data forwarding (bm_parse_opts appending unknown tokens) is never executed against the kernel.

requirements.behavior: Failure status and diagnostic for a rejected mount: a missing target, an unknown fstype without probing, and an invalid data token such as size=bogus, compared with util-linux mount status classes.
requirements.gap: No failing mount request is executed. Usage-error parsing (-t/-o without a value, conflicting verbs) is not exercised either.

requirements.behavior: No host mount changes: every mount is confined to the per-side namespace and is gone after the side ends.
requirements.gap: No driver-side post-condition check exists, because no driver runs mounts.

entries.notes: Source: loadables/bashmount.c:80-131 (option table and data forwarding) and :360-386 (bm_do_mount; the fs-type probe is skipped for bind/remount). Without -t, the candidate probes every type in /proc/filesystems (bm_probe_types, :338). util-linux uses libmount/blkid instead, so an untyped mount may diverge. Locked-flag semantics differ when the namespace is created inside a user namespace: remounting away MNT_LOCK_* flags inherited from the parent fails with EPERM. Use a fresh tmpfs created inside the namespace so no flags are locked.

original.purpose: Exercise ordinary, lazy, and force unmount flag mapping and observable cleanup.
original.reason: Requires a disposable VM with disposable private-namespace mounts, or a reviewed umount2(2) mock that records flags. Verify normal, -l/MNT_DETACH, and -f/MNT_FORCE calls and cleanup/error behavior; no unmount operation is run in this suite.

entries.current_reason: Missing fixture. No executed case attempts a mount. In the existing drivers uid 2000 gets EPERM from mount(2), but a fresh user plus mount namespace (USERNS) gives namespace-scoped CAP_SYS_ADMIN, enough for tmpfs mounts, binds, remounts and lazy unmounts of mounts created there. Locked-flag rules apply only to mounts inherited from the parent namespace, so use fresh tmpfs mounts. A real MNT_FORCE needs initial-namespace CAP_SYS_ADMIN, so its flag mapping is captured with SECCOMP-NOTIFY instead.

requirements.behavior: -u DST performs an ordinary unmount: the mount disappears from mountinfo and the DST directory remains.
-u -l DST requests MNT_DETACH. With an open descriptor inside DST (exec 3<dst/file) a normal unmount fails with EBUSY, while -l succeeds, detaches DST from mountinfo, and leaves fd 3 readable.
-u -f DST requests MNT_FORCE, and the status and cleanup are compared with `umount -f`.
requirements.gap: A real MNT_FORCE needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the initial user namespace (the capable() check in ksys_umount), which USERNS does not give. The flag mapping (-f gives MNT_FORCE=1, -l gives MNT_DETACH=2) can be recorded by SECCOMP-NOTIFY in the modern plain driver, which captures umount2(target, flags) and replies with success or an error for both util-linux `umount -f` and the candidate, without reaching the kernel.

requirements.behavior: Error behavior: unmounting a non-mountpoint (EINVAL), a missing path (ENOENT), and a busy mount without -l (EBUSY), with nonzero status and diagnostics compared with util-linux umount status classes.
Observable cleanup: after each side, no fixture mount remains in the namespace.

entries.notes: Source: loadables/bashmount.c:389-395 (bm_do_umount) and :547-556 (-l means MNT_DETACH only after -u; otherwise it lists; -f is rejected without -u). The parse-only paths (-f without -u returns EX_USAGE) are reachable unprivileged and are not yet executed.

requirements.gap: Same capability; existing -h cases only reapply the caller's own identity.

entries.notes: Candidate: loadables/chown.c:44 getpwnam, :59 getgrnam, :97-98 chown/lchown. No observed mismatch in executed identity-preserving cases.

requirements.behavior: Command arguments are forwarded unchanged (spaces, empty arg, leading dash) and the command is found by execvp
Child exit status and signal death propagate as chrt's status (e.g. exit 7 gives 7; SIGTERM gives the shell-visible 143)

entries.notes: loadables/chrt.c:346 bchrt_run_command, :289 bchrt_set_pid. The policy is set in the forked child before execvp, so the shell itself is never re-scheduled. SCHED_RESET_ON_FORK is 0x40000000. Unprivileged Linux may switch its own task among OTHER/BATCH/IDLE; IDLE to OTHER is allowed when RLIMIT_NICE permits (since 2.6.39).

entries.current_reason: Not executed. Two concrete blockers. (1) The update helper hard-codes /bin/bash, which in the parity VM is the GNU reference shell, so the candidate always takes the 'pkg unavailable' path unless the image installs the candidate as /bin/bash. original.purpose: Exercise hard-link permission checks across an ownership boundary.

The provided fixtures use one unprivileged identity; do not alter host users, ownership, or kernel policy.

requirements.behavior: With fs.protected_hardlinks=1, a hard link by uid 2000 to a regular file owned by another uid, which the caller cannot read and write, fails with EPERM, a diagnostic and no destination. Match GNU link.
requirements.gap: No fixture file owned by another uid exists. Creating one needs CAP_CHOWN, and all fixture files are owned by 2000.

requirements.behavior: The protected-hardlinks policy exception: linking a differently owned file the caller can read and write (mode 0666) succeeds.
The source lives in a sticky world-writable directory, as stated in the scenario.
requirements.gap: A sticky directory owned by another uid needs root setup.

requirements.behavior: The policy is known and controlled: protected_hardlinks is read before each side, and the 0 setting (link allowed) is covered with a restore.
requirements.gap: Reading /proc/sys/fs/protected_hardlinks is unprivileged, but writing it needs root plus restore.

entries.notes: The modern tree() records mode but not owner, so either add the uid to the snapshot or assert ownership semantically. Only the policy-0 variant needs KSTATE; r1-r3 need SYNTH-IDENT alone. USERNS cannot substitute here: without newuidmap (uidmap is not installed), an unprivileged user namespace maps only uid 2000, so no file with a second real owner can exist.

original.purpose: Future verification of become's token handling, supplementary groups, uid/gid transition, environment, working directory, and exec arguments.
original.reason: Requires a disposable privileged VM with controlled test identities, a reviewed kernel auth-token mock, and a harmless instrumented target shell to observe credential and exec state. This fixture runner intentionally provides neither privilege nor an auth device.

entries.current_reason: become is root-only by design and its token path depends on the bash-os kernel auth device. Only the non-root refusal is observable by an ordinary fixture.

requirements.behavior: become refuses unless the real uid is 0, with no partial change
requirements.gap: No fixture. Observable unprivileged: as uid 2000, login become USER must fail with 'only root may drop privileges' and status 1 (login.c:1615).

requirements.behavior: Kernel auth-token handling: --auth-fd N reads 32 token bytes and ioctl CONSUME on /dev/bashos-auth; --auth-token HEX is accepted with a deprecation warning; a rejected token aborts before any uid/gid change
requirements.gap: Requires the bash-os kernel auth device /dev/bashos-auth (BL_AUTH_IOC_MINT/CONSUME ioctls, login.c:107, :262). The Debian VM kernel has no such device, and no unprivileged fixture can mint or consume a kernel token. Only the 'no open /dev/bashos-auth fd' rejection path is observable without it.

requirements.behavior: setgroups to the primary group only (or with --with-supplementary), setresgid then setresuid to the target, observed in the exec'd process
requirements.gap: Requires the fixture side to run with real uid 0 (become checks getuid()==0). uid 2000 cannot call setresuid to another identity, so the transition cannot be observed unprivileged.

original.purpose: Validate mlockall(MCL_CURRENT|MCL_FUTURE) success and its RLIMIT_MEMLOCK failure path, including whether failure leaves process state unchanged.
original.reason: Requires a disposable Linux VM or reviewed mlockall/getrlimit syscall mock with a controlled RLIMIT_MEMLOCK, observable VmLck before and after, and guaranteed process teardown. The operation locks the shell's current and future pages, so it is not invoked by this fixture suite.

entries.current_reason: The failure paths need no privilege and have no fixture. The success path needs a per-case RLIMIT_MEMLOCK at least as large as the shell's mapped size. Raising the hard limit needs CAP_SYS_RESOURCE (setrlimit returns EPERM under uid 2000), so the fixture cannot set it itself. RLIMIT_MEMLOCK in both the legacy runner and the plain driver is inherited from the guest default (kernel default 8 MiB, not pinned by either driver). Lowering it with `ulimit -l` is unprivileged. Raising the hard limit needs CAP_SYS_RESOURCE, which only the root controller holds. Not a privilege block for the fixture: the guest controller already runs as root and sets rlimits in terminal.child_limits before setuid(2000), so a per-case RLIMIT_MEMLOCK option there is a small existing-driver extension (root-owned), not a new privileged driver.

requirements.behavior: mlock all with a sufficient RLIMIT_MEMLOCK succeeds (status 0) and VmLck becomes > 0 and >= resident set; later allocations are locked (MCL_FUTURE)
requirements.gap: No case. Whether the guest default limit (8 MiB) suffices for mlockall of the 15 MB static candidate mappings is unknown; a deterministic success needs the controller to set the limit per case.

requirements.behavior: With a soft limit below the resident size, the candidate pre-check fails: "rlimit: needed=N soft=S hard=H - set ulimit -l before continuing", status 1, VmLck unchanged (0)
If mlockall itself fails (EAGAIN/ENOMEM after the pre-check passes) the diagnostic plus "current RLIMIT_MEMLOCK: soft=.. hard=.." is printed and status 1; no pages remain locked
Process teardown releases the locks (side exits)
requirements.gap: Implicit in per-side processes; not asserted.

entries.notes: Candidate: bm_all_cmd loadables/mlock.c:112-139, pre-check bm_check_rlimit_for :71-89 (needed = statm resident * page). RLIMIT_MEMLOCK in both the legacy runner and the plain driver is inherited from the guest default (kernel default 8 MiB, not pinned by either driver). Lowering it with `ulimit -l` is unprivileged. Raising the hard limit needs CAP_SYS_RESOURCE, which only the root controller holds. original.purpose: Check cgroup v2 create, controller value, process membership, controller-enable, and remove behavior.

entries.current_reason: Writing cgroup files needs a writable delegated subtree. As uid 2000, mkdir under root-owned /sys/fs/cgroup returns EACCES; the legacy runner has no /sys. The root controller must create a per-side subtree and chown it to uid 2000 (cgroup delegation: directory, cgroup.procs, cgroup.subtree_control). The candidate hardcodes /sys/fs/cgroup (loadables/ns.c:532), so the fixture must address the subtree by its relative path from the root. Path validation needs no privilege.

original.purpose: Check deny-setgroups ordering and uid_map/gid_map writes for a fresh user namespace.
original.reason: Requires a disposable VM and a fresh user namespace mapped only to synthetic test IDs. Independently inspect the kernel's uid_map, gid_map, and setgroups interfaces after valid writes, then compare invalid ranges and ordering failures. Do not change host identity mappings or accounts.

entries.current_reason: Not a capability block. Writing maps for one's own fresh user namespace is unprivileged. Unprivileged user namespaces make every namespace operation here reachable for uid 2000 in the modern plain driver, which has no seccomp filter and no userns restriction. A new user namespace grants CAP_SYS_ADMIN over namespaces, mounts and maps it owns, and the effects stay confined to the disposable side process. The legacy runner cannot host these cases because bwrap --disable-userns makes CLONE_NEWUSER fail. Preflight: record /proc/sys/user/max_user_namespaces and kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone (Debian), and ERROR if creation fails. Reference oracle: util-linux 2.41 unshare/nsenter/mount/findmnt in the guest, plus /proc/self/ns/*, /proc/self/mountinfo, /proc/self/uid_map|gid_map|setgroups and /proc/self/status read by the side's own processes. No fixture exists.

original.purpose: Verify the NTS-KE negotiation, cookie handling and authenticated NTP response path against independently generated protocol fixtures.
original.reason: Requires local TLS NTS-KE and UDP NTP mock peers in a future disposable VM with a private network namespace, with test-only certificates/keys and an independent RFC 8915 plus AES-SIV-CMAC fixture generator/verifier. requirements.gap: No executed case contacts an NTS-KE server; no TLS peer with a fixture CA exists.

requirements.behavior: Cookies returned by NTS-KE are consumed: the NTP request carries Unique Identifier, NTS Cookie (and placeholder) extension fields and an authenticator sealed with the exported C2S key.
requirements.gap: No recorded NTP request bytes from the candidate exist; no independent AES-SIV-CMAC verifier has run.

original.purpose: Verify multi-server offset aggregation, panic/clamp boundaries and the documented -n applied=no result.

original.purpose: Exercise pack cat through an index v2 64-bit offset entry above the 32-bit offset range.

original.purpose: Validate accepted seed sizes, durable consume-before-credit ordering, exact credit payload, and nonblocking refresh behavior.
original.reason: Requires a disposable VM with a dedicated random pool and explicit privilege/capability setup, or a mock that intercepts RNDADDENTROPY and getrandom. The future test must capture the exact seed bytes and credit count, prove unlink plus directory fsync precedes credit, and avoid the host kernel entropy pool entirely.

entries.current_reason: Not a capability block for most obligations. save uses only getrandom and file operations, both allowed in the legacy runner. RNDADDENTROPY needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the initial user namespace, so under uid 2000 the kernel returns EPERM and the credit-denial path is reachable now. A SECCOMP-NOTIFY helper (modern plain driver only; trusted python3: fork, the child sets no_new_privs and installs a seccomp filter with SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_NEW_LISTENER for openat/unlinkat/renameat/fsync/ioctl/getrandom, passes the listener fd to the parent via SCM_RIGHTS, then execs the side shell; the parent records every notified call in order and either continues it or answers with a chosen return value) records ordering and injects faults or successes without privilege. It also lets the supervisor answer RNDADDENTROPY with success, a closed mock at the kernel boundary. Only the real-kernel credit acceptance needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN, since RNDADDENTROPY returns EPERM under uid 2000.

requirements.behavior: Accepted seed sizes 32..4096 bytes (512 typical); 31 and 4097 rejected without consumption
Consume before credit: unlinkat(FILE) and fsync(dir) happen before ioctl(RNDADDENTROPY)
Exact credit payload: rand_pool_info.buf_size == n, buf == seed bytes, entropy_count == min(8n, poolsize)
requirements.gap: Needs argument capture; supervisor reads the struct from the notified process memory (/proc/PID/mem, parent of the traced shell under Yama scope 1).

requirements.behavior: After a successful credit, a nonblocking getrandom refresh rewrites FILE (n bytes, 0600) via temp+rename
requirements.gap: Success needs either a real credit (CAP_SYS_ADMIN) or a mocked success answer.

requirements.behavior: Real kernel acceptance of the credit (ioctl returns 0)
requirements.gap: Needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the initial user namespace (PRIV-ROOT); on 6.12 the pool effect is not otherwise observable (entropy_avail saturates at 256), so only the return value is checkable.

requirements.behavior: Missing FILE: "no seed at FILE (first boot)" on stderr, exit 0
requirements.gap: Reachable now in the legacy runner.

original.purpose: Exercise invalid seed files, credit denial, post-consumption refresh failures, and restoration/cleanup paths.
original.reason: Requires a disposable VM or syscall/filesystem fault-injection mock that can deny entropy credit and inject read, sync, rename, and getrandom failures. Verify invalid files are untouched and never credited, failed credit restores identical uncredited bytes when restoration succeeds, consumed bytes are never reusable after refresh failure, and no temporary file or FD is leaked. Power-cut durability additionally needs filesystem crash/recovery testing in a disposable VM.

entries.current_reason: Not a capability block for most obligations. save uses only getrandom and file operations, both allowed in the legacy runner. RNDADDENTROPY needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the initial user namespace, so under uid 2000 the kernel returns EPERM and the credit-denial path is reachable now. A SECCOMP-NOTIFY helper (modern plain driver only; trusted python3: fork, the child sets no_new_privs and installs a seccomp filter with SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_NEW_LISTENER for openat/unlinkat/renameat/fsync/ioctl/getrandom, passes the listener fd to the parent via SCM_RIGHTS, then execs the side shell; the parent records every notified call in order and either continues it or answers with a chosen return value) records ordering and injects faults or successes without privilege. It also lets the supervisor answer RNDADDENTROPY with success, a closed mock at the kernel boundary. Only power-cut durability needs a new driver capability: an abrupt guest reset during the operation (VM-LIFECYCLE) on a persistent filesystem (BLOCK-DEV). A fixture cannot crash the kernel or bypass page-cache semantics.

requirements.behavior: Invalid seed files are untouched and never credited: wrong mode (0644), symlink, hardlink (nlink 2), non-regular (directory/FIFO), size out of range -> status 1 with diagnostic, file still present

requirements.gap: No case; reachable in the legacy runner now because the kernel denies RNDADDENTROPY without CAP_SYS_ADMIN.

requirements.behavior: Restore failure after denied credit is reported ("restore ...") and the seed is not left half-written
requirements.gap: Needs injected renameat/fsync failure during restore.

requirements.behavior: Refresh failure after a successful credit (getrandom EAGAIN or write failure): consumed bytes are never written back
requirements.gap: Needs mocked credit success plus injected getrandom/rename failure (SECCOMP-NOTIFY).

requirements.behavior: Injected read/sync/rename failures leave no temp file and no leaked descriptor (/proc/self/fd count unchanged in the shell)
Power-cut durability: after abrupt VM reset between consume and credit, the seed is not reusable
requirements.gap: Needs VM-LIFECYCLE with an abrupt reset (QMP system_reset or kill) and BLOCK-DEV on a journaled filesystem image; tmpfs cannot model crash durability.

entries.notes: Candidate: do_load loadables/rngseed.c:189-256 (restore via write_seed on credit failure :222-227), read_seed checks :113-138.

original.purpose: Full GNU comparison of batch arithmetic, ordering, and malformed-row handling against the same controlled slabinfo data.
original.reason: Requires a disposable VM or reviewed syscall/file-open mock that redirects both candidate and procps-ng slabtop reads of /proc/slabinfo to the same private fixture. GNU slabtop does not honor BASHOS_PROC_ROOT, while the provided runner cannot mount or interpose a shared mock. entries.current_reason: Never executed against procps slabtop. GNU slabtop reads /proc/slabinfo only (root-readable 0400 on the live kernel) and takes no input path. A per-side unprivileged user+mount namespace with a fixture bind-mounted over /proc/slabinfo gives both implementations the same readable data without guest root. Precondition for root: confirm unprivileged user namespaces in the guest's case context. The evaluation runs under systemd-run plus unshare --mount --pid --net --mount-proc as root and drops to uid 2000. The case must belong to a modern VM group, not the legacy bubblewrap runner, which passes --disable-userns. user.max_user_namespaces must be nonzero (it is on the Debian default kernel).

entries.notes: The legacy exclusions state this explicitly. slabtop.c reads BASHOS_PROC_ROOT/slabinfo. The candidate's default-root path is also exercised once the overlay exists. Kernel rules (fs/namespace.c, Linux 6.12): after unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNS) the copied mounts, including the guest's /proc, are MNT_LOCKED. Locking forbids unmounting or moving them and revealing what lies beneath. It does not forbid mounting on top. A bind mount goes through do_loopback, which requires only may_mount (CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the userns that owns the new mount namespace, which the unshare -U caller has) and a source in the caller's namespace. mount_too_revealing()/mnt_already_visible() is checked only in do_new_mount for new instances of SB_I_USERNS_VISIBLE filesystems (proc, sysfs), so it does not apply to a bind mount over one file such as /proc/meminfo or /proc/slabinfo. This is the mechanism unprivileged-container lxcfs overlays rely on. I did not run it on a host (kernel and namespace tests are VM-only). (b) procps slabtop opens /proc/slabinfo by path, so it reads the bind-mounted fixture. The fixture is mode 0644 and owned by the caller, so the root-only permission of the live file no longer matters. Earlier rating requires_capability, revised.

Many keys are per-namespace and deterministic in a fresh namespace, identical for both sides: kernel.hostname (bwrap sets 'parity'), kernel.domainname, net.ipv4.ip_default_ttl / net.ipv4.ip_forward in the fresh netns, fs.mqueue.msg_max and kernel.shmmni in the fresh IPC ns, kernel.ostype, kernel.osrelease. A USERNS in the plain driver owns its UTS/net/IPC namespaces, so writes to those namespaced keys are permitted and confined to it. A per-side bind mount of a fixture tree over /proc/sys, or of fixture dirs over /etc/sysctl.d and siblings, in the child's mount namespace (preflight) gives a fixed tree for both candidate and procps, which both hardcode /proc/sys. Candidate: bsc_load_system loadables/sysctl.c:497-515, bsc_load_file/bsc_load_dir_sorted :406-495.

original.purpose: Qualify the documented read retry path when an attribute grows between the size probe and data read.
original.reason: Requires a deterministic syscall interposer or mock that can force ERANGE and control successive getxattr sizes. Do not substitute an uncontrolled concurrent writer race; run this later with a dedicated disposable VM/mock fixture.

entries.current_reason: Argument matching in a stateless filter is enough for the retry and exhaustion paths, so no mock driver is needed for them. Only a probe that changes between calls needs a stateful supervisor.

requirements.behavior: After a successful size probe, an ERANGE on the data read triggers a re-probe and a larger buffer, and the value is returned intact.
requirements.gap: Not executed. A stateless per-side /usr/bin/python3 helper that sets PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS and installs a stateless seccomp BPF filter through ctypes prctl(PR_SET_SECCOMP, SECCOMP_MODE_FILTER) returning SECCOMP_RET_ERRNO|E for a named syscall (optionally only when an argument equals a chosen value), then execs the side's shell `$BASH -c BODY`; unprivileged, inherited across exec, applies identically to GNU and candidate, and needs no new driver (the VM plain driver installs no filter of its own) can return ERANGE only for getxattr calls whose size argument equals the probed size n. The retry asks for max(new probe, 2n) = 2n (xattr.c:121-134), which passes the filter, so the growth path runs deterministically without a racing writer.
